items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: And even the critics like Gunther Schuller and so on who make statements like that without a genuine understanding of what happened.

ctx.x: Wasn't he good at drawing out the best in his musicians? For instance, many of whom were New Orleans musicians. Wasn't he talented in the way he placed them and in the way in which he brought them out to their forms?

I don't think so. I don't think he contributed to that. I think that whoever happened to be functioning as concertmaster and as man, and I think that whoever happened to be doing the arrangements were the people who were responsible for that. And he did have great people. You see, there's no question about that. But the fact that he had great people does not make him a great composer. He was certainly not a great musician. I think even his closest associates would agree to that. And that his major contribution…
Well, of course, Gunther Schuller wrote a whole book on musical development.
